question.text: This word describes the illegal production and sale of liquor during Prohibition. It also applies to anything taken without permission and distributed for profit.
question.clue: The Purple Gang in Detroit had a major influence on this industry, which imported its main product from Belle Isle and Windsor.

swap.text: Created in response to the Supreme Court case of Pollock vs. Farmer's Loan and Trust, this amendment created the federal income tax.
swap.clue: It was introduced by Sereno Payne in order to fulfill a debate promise, and when it unexpectedly passed the Senate, Payne began lobbying against its ratification.

question.text: The Italian-American Mafia rose to prominence by selling bootleg alcohol following the passage of this policy, which outlawed the consumption and sale of alcohol.
question.clue: Wayne Wheeler drafted a bill that would enforce this policy.

swap.leadin: In 1914, Woodrow Wilson ordered this man to lead the expedition to capture Pancho Villa.
swap.text: Name this General of the Armies, nicknamed "Blackjack."
swap.clue: This American general was ordered by President Wilson to find Villa following the raid. He was recalled shortly thereafter and was appointed the leader of the American Expeditionary Force in World War I.

question.leadin: This man paid his way through Hampton Institute by working as a janitor.
question.text: Name this civil rights leader of the early 20th century and first president of the Tuskegee Institute. This man advocated for gradual social change in contrast to W.E.B. Du Bois.
question.clue: The most famous student of Sam C. Armstrong, this founder of the National Negro Business League urged everyone to "Cast down your bucket where you are" in a speech.

swap.text: This author formulated his "Frontier Thesis," which stated that Westward expansion had been essential to the formation of American democracy.
swap.clue: In one essay, this historian discussed the "three waves" of settlement in the West, and blamed its individualism for the spoils system.

question.text: Taft tried running for re-election, but the concurrent run of Theodore Roosevelt under this personal party named for an animal allowed Woodrow Wilson to come out on top.
question.clue: Perhaps the greatest electoral successes of a party by this name came earlier, in California, where Hiram Johnson was elected governor and then Senator on its banner.

swap.leadin: Deborah Blum's The Poison Squad focuses on the work of Dr. Harvey Washington Wiley, who is often known as the "father" of this law.
swap.text: Name this act which regulated sanitary standards and prohibited the mislabeling of certain consumables. It was passed alongside the Meat Inspection Act.
swap.clue: This legislation was passed due to lobbying by Harvey Washington Wiley, and a major proponent of it was Indiana Senator Albert Beveridge.

question.leadin: The prosecutor in this case was particularly upset that the defendant believed that Man evolved "not even from American monkeys but from old world ones."
question.text: Name this 1925 case that concerned the teaching of the theory of evolution.
question.answerHtml: Scopes Monkey Trial [or The State of Tennessee v. John Thomas Scopes]
question.clue: Broadcast over WGN Radio, it addressed a violation of the Butler Act and was presided over by John Raulston.

swap.leadin: This man advocated for the entry of blacks into labor unions in his journal, The Messenger.
swap.text: Name this early civil rights leader who founded the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters.
swap.clue: While at City College and with the help of Chandler Owen he founded the radical magazine that he used as his bully pulpit.

question.leadin: Name these 20th-century U.S. Vice Presidents, FTSNOP.
question.text: F15P, this vice president to Herbert Hoover is most famous for being vice president to Hoover.
question.clue: This man's comment "good times are just around the corner" was misattributed to his superior, contributing to an election loss in 1932.

swap.text: The deportation of Goodman and Berkman occurred as part of the "raids" conducted by this Attorney General during the Red Scare.
swap.clue: Acting Secretary of Labor Louis Post undid many of this man's actions, which included a crackdown on the Union of Russian Workers for producing an anarchist manifesto.

question.leadin: The Supreme Court case [this person] v. Fessenden ruled that he could be charged in state court despite already having pled guilty in federal court.
question.text: Name this person, whose most famous action began with him buying and reselling postal reply coupons.
question.answerHtml: Charles Ponzi [accept Carlo Pietro Giovanni Guglielmo Tebaldo Ponzi]
question.clue: Clarence Barron's expose in the Boston Post calculated that this man must have purchased 160 million items, out of a worldwide supply of only 27,000, for his claimed strategy to work.

swap.text: The greatest project of the Sui dynasty was a project of this type designed to connect northern and southern China by water. Jimmy Carter signed over a US-owned project of this type to Omar Torrijos in 1979.
swap.clue: Yellow fever afflicted workers who built one of these structures across the Isthmus of Darien.

question.leadin: Helena Dudley and Vida Scudder were forced from their positions at one of these institutions to support the Bread and Roses Strike.
question.text: Name these institutions which were inspired by London's Toynbee Hall. Alice Hamilton worked as a doctor at one of these institutions.
question.clue: The first one, founded by Samuel Barnett, inspired Stanton Coit to bring the idea to the U.S. in the form of the Neighborhood Guild in New York.

swap.text: The financial crisis of 1914 was handled by this Wilsonian Secretary of the Treasury who implemented the New Freedom program. He saw his initial lead and his hopes for the Democratic Presidential nomination gradually slip away at the 1924 "Klanbake convention."
swap.clue: Though he led on the first ballot, his political hopes were dashed for a second time at the Klanbake Convention, where he was supported by the KKK, and both he and his rival Al Smith lost the nomination to John W. Davis.

question.text: Joseph Foraker broke with the Roosevelt Administration after this 1906 scandal, where 167 black soldiers were dishonorably discharged on charges of shooting a white bartender in the namesake Texas city. Foraker unsuccessfully fought for the men to be reinstated, and modern historians generally believe they were framed by planted evidence.

swap.text: In 1924, La Follette ran for President on the Progressive ticket, with this Democratic senator from a northern state as his running-mate.

question.text: In 1883, Willard wrote this document which encouraged leaders worldwide to oppose the trades in alcohol and opium, and then sent Mary Clement Leavitt on a world tour promoting this document.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some related American politicians.
swap.text: This Chicago politician introduced the Pure Food and Drug Act in the House in 1906, but is better known for another piece of legislation that forbid the transportation of women across state lines for immoral purposes.
swap.clue: This politician was the House sponsor of the Pure Food and Drug Act, as well as the co-sponsor of a bill expanding the ICC's power over railroads with Stephen Elkins. For 15 points, name this Illinois representative whose name is often applied to his 1910 White-Slave Traffic Act outlawing the transportation of women over state lines for immoral purposes.
